# Salary Slip Format in India 2026: Every Component Explained with Real Examples


October 13, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/salary-slip-format-in-india-2026-every-component-explained-with-real-examples/#respond)


A salary slip is more than a piece of paper your HR department hands you at the end of the month. It is the single most important financial document for any salaried employee in India.


You need it to apply for a home loan. Banks ask for it before approving a credit card. Embassies require it for visa applications. Landlords want to see it before signing a rental agreement. And when you switch jobs, your new employer uses it to verify your previous compensation.


Yet most employees in India cannot fully read their own salary slip. Terms like “special allowance,” “conveyance allowance,” or “employer PF contribution” appear on the payslip every month without any clear explanation. On the employer side, many small business owners create salary slips using outdated Excel templates that miss mandatory components or show incorrect calculations.


This guide breaks down every single component of a salary slip in India, explains what each line item means, shows you how it is calculated, and gives you the correct format that meets legal requirements in 2026.


## What Is a Salary Slip?


A salary slip (also called a payslip or wage slip) is a document issued by an employer to an employee every month. It shows the detailed breakdown of how the employee’s salary was calculated, including all earnings, deductions, and the final amount credited to their bank account.


### Why a Salary Slip Matters


Purpose Why It Is Needed


Income proof for loans Banks and NBFCs require 3 to 6 months of salary slips for home loans, car loans, and personal loans


Visa applications Most embassies require recent salary slips as proof of financial stability


Rental agreements Landlords use salary slips to verify a tenant’s ability to pay rent


Job switching New employers verify previous CTC and salary structure from the last payslip


Tax filing Employees use salary slips to verify TDS deductions and file income tax returns


PF withdrawal EPFO may ask for salary slips to verify contribution amounts


Legal disputes Salary slips serve as evidence in labour disputes and court proceedings


Credit card applications Banks assess repayment capacity from salary slip details


### Is a Salary Slip Mandatory in India?


Yes. While the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 does not explicitly use the term “salary slip,” state level Shops and Establishments Acts across India require employers to provide a written statement of wages to employees. Several states have prescribed specific formats:


State Requirement Prescribed Form


Tamil Nadu Mandatory payslip for all establishments Form T


Karnataka Mandatory wage slip for contract workers Form XIX


Maharashtra Wage statement required As per Maharashtra S&E Rules


Delhi Wage statement required As per Delhi S&E Act


All states (upcoming) Mandatory under Code on Wages, 2019 Prescribed format (when notified)


The Code on Wages, 2019 (once fully notified) will make salary slips mandatory for all employers across India, with a prescribed format covering all essential components.


## The Standard Salary Slip Format: 5 Sections Every Payslip Must Have


A properly formatted salary slip in India contains five distinct sections. Each section serves a specific purpose.


### Section 1: Company and Employee Information (Header)


This section identifies who issued the payslip and for whom.


Field Description Example


Company name Legal name of the employer Sharma Manufacturing Pvt. Ltd.


Company address Registered office address 45, Industrial Area, Phase II, Pune 411018


Company logo Optional but professional (Logo)


Employee name Full legal name as per records Rajesh Kumar Sharma


Employee ID Unique identification number EMP0042


Designation Current job title Senior Accountant


Department Department or team Finance


Date of joining The employee’s start date March 15, 2022


Pay period Month and year for this salary September 2026


Payment date Actual date salary was credited October 5, 2026


Bank account number Last 4 digits (masked for security) XXXX XXXX 4521


PAN number Employee’s PAN ABCPS1234F


UAN number Universal Account Number for PF 101234567890


ESI number (if applicable) ESI IP number 3112345678


### Section 2: Earnings (Left Side of the Payslip)


This section lists everything the employee earns before any deductions.


### Section 3: Deductions (Right Side of the Payslip)


This section lists everything deducted from the gross salary.


### Section 4: Summary (Bottom)


This section shows the final calculation: Gross Earnings minus Total Deductions equals Net Pay.


### Section 5: Footer


This includes the employer’s authorized signature (or digital authentication), a note that the payslip is system generated, and any disclaimers.


We will now explain every component in Sections 2 and 3 in complete detail.


## Every Earnings Component Explained


Here is a detailed explanation of every earnings component that appears on an Indian salary slip, along with how each one is calculated.


### 1. Basic Salary


Aspect Details


What it is The core fixed component of your salary, before any allowances or bonuses


Typical percentage 40% to 50% of CTC (many companies keep it at 40% to reduce PF liability)


Why it matters PF contribution, gratuity, HRA exemption, and leave encashment are all calculated on basic salary


Tax treatment Fully taxable under both old and new tax regimes


Regulatory note Under the Code on Wages, 2019 (when notified), basic salary plus DA must be at least 50% of total remuneration


**Calculation Example:** If CTC is ₹6,00,000 per year and basic is 40% of CTC: Basic Salary = ₹6,00,000 × 40% = ₹2,40,000 per year = ₹20,000 per month


### 2. House Rent Allowance (HRA)


Aspect Details


What it is An allowance paid to employees to cover house rent expenses


Typical percentage 50% of basic in metro cities (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata), 40% of basic in non metro cities


Tax treatment Partially exempt under Section 10(13A) of the Income Tax Act


**HRA Tax Exemption Calculation:** The exempt amount is the lowest of these three:


Calculation Formula Example (Basic ₹20,000, Rent ₹10,000, Metro City)


Actual HRA received As per salary structure ₹10,000


50% of basic (metro) or 40% (non metro) Basic × 50% or 40% ₹20,000 × 50% = ₹10,000


Rent paid minus 10% of basic Rent minus (Basic × 10%) ₹10,000 minus ₹2,000 = ₹8,000


**Exempt HRA = ₹8,000** (lowest of the three) **Taxable HRA = ₹10,000 minus ₹8,000 = ₹2,000**


**Important for the New Tax Regime:** HRA exemption is NOT available under the new tax regime (Section 115BAC). Employees who choose the new regime pay tax on the full HRA amount.


### 3. Dearness Allowance (DA)


Aspect Details


What it is An inflation adjustment component linked to the Consumer Price Index (CPI)


Where it applies Primarily in government and public sector jobs; less common in private sector


Typical percentage Revised periodically by the government; currently around 50% of basic for central government employees


Tax treatment Fully taxable


PF impact DA is added to basic for PF calculation purposes (PF is calculated on Basic + DA)


Most private sector companies in India do not include DA as a separate component. Instead, they adjust for inflation through annual increments to the basic salary or special allowance.


### 4. Conveyance Allowance (Transport Allowance)


Aspect Details


What it is An allowance to cover daily commute expenses


Typical amount ₹1,600 per month for regular employees; ₹3,200 per month for differently abled employees


Tax treatment Under the old tax regime, ₹1,600/month was exempt (now subsumed into the standard deduction of ₹75,000 for AY 2026-27)


Current status Many companies still show it as a separate line item even though the old exemption has been replaced by the standard deduction


### 5. Special Allowance


Aspect Details


What it is A catch all component that absorbs the remaining CTC after basic, HRA, and other fixed allowances


Typical percentage Varies widely; usually 20% to 40% of CTC


Tax treatment Fully taxable under both tax regimes


Why companies use it Flexibility to structure CTC without creating too many separate components


**Calculation Example:** If monthly CTC is ₹50,000, Basic is ₹20,000, HRA is ₹10,000, and employer PF is ₹2,400: Special Allowance = ₹50,000 minus ₹20,000 minus ₹10,000 minus ₹2,400 = ₹17,600


### 6. Leave Travel Allowance (LTA)


Aspect Details


What it is An allowance for travel expenses during leave


Tax treatment Exempt under Section 10(5) for actual travel costs within India (2 journeys in a block of 4 calendar years). Only domestic travel; international travel is not covered


Current block 2026 to 2029 (January 2026 to December 2029)


Claiming exemption Employee must submit travel bills (tickets only, not hotel or food expenses)


New tax regime LTA exemption is NOT available under the new tax regime


### 7. Medical Allowance


Aspect Details


What it is A fixed monthly allowance for medical expenses


Old exemption ₹15,000 per year was exempt (discontinued from FY 2018-19)


Current status Fully taxable; the old exemption has been replaced by the standard deduction


Common practice Many companies have merged medical allowance into special allowance


### 8. Children Education Allowance


Aspect Details


What it is An allowance for children’s school education expenses


Exemption ₹100 per month per child, maximum 2 children (₹2,400 per year total)


Tax treatment Exempt up to the limit under the old tax regime; fully taxable under the new regime


Practical note The exemption amount has not been revised in decades and is largely symbolic


### 9. Other Common Allowances


Allowance What It Covers Typical Amount Tax Treatment


Telephone/Mobile allowance Work related phone and internet expenses ₹1,000 to ₹3,000/month Exempt if bills submitted (old regime)


Food/Meal allowance Meal expenses during work hours Up to ₹50 per meal (Sodexo/meal cards) Exempt up to ₹2,200/month via meal cards


Uniform allowance Cost of work uniforms Actual cost Exempt if genuinely for uniform


Shift allowance Extra pay for night or rotating shifts ₹500 to ₹3,000/month Fully taxable


Performance bonus Variable pay based on performance Varies Fully taxable


Overtime pay Pay for hours worked beyond normal duty 2x normal wage rate (Factories Act) Fully taxable


Arrears Back pay from a salary revision or correction Varies Taxable in the year of receipt; relief under Section 89 available


### Complete Earnings Summary Table


Here is what a typical salary slip’s earnings section looks like for an employee with a monthly CTC of ₹50,000:


Earnings Component Monthly Amount


Basic Salary ₹20,000


House Rent Allowance (HRA) ₹10,000


Special Allowance ₹13,200


Conveyance Allowance ₹1,600


Medical Allowance ₹1,250


Children Education Allowance ₹200


**Total Gross Earnings** **₹46,250**


Note: The remaining ₹3,750 from the ₹50,000 CTC goes toward employer PF contribution (₹2,400), employer ESI contribution (if applicable), and EDLI/admin charges. These are employer costs, not employee earnings.


## Every Deduction Component Explained


Now let us look at the right side of the salary slip, where deductions are listed.


### 1. Provident Fund (PF) Employee Contribution


Aspect Details


What it is Mandatory retirement savings deducted from the employee’s salary


Rate 12% of Basic Salary (plus DA, if applicable)


Wage ceiling Statutory calculation is on basic up to ₹15,000 per month. Employers may choose to calculate on actual basic if higher


Applicability Mandatory for establishments with 20 or more employees


Tax treatment Deductible under Section 80C (old regime) up to ₹1,50,000 per year


**Calculation Example:** If Basic Salary = ₹20,000 and employer calculates PF on the full amount: Employee PF = ₹20,000 × 12% = ₹2,400 per month


If employer restricts PF to the ₹15,000 statutory ceiling: Employee PF = ₹15,000 × 12% = ₹1,800 per month


**What Happens to the Employer’s PF Contribution?**


Component Rate Goes To


Employer PF contribution 3.67% of Basic Employee’s PF account


Employer Pension contribution (EPS) 8.33% of Basic (capped at ₹15,000) Employee Pension Scheme


EDLI (Employer Deposit Linked Insurance) 0.50% of Basic Life insurance for employee


PF admin charges 0.50% of Basic EPFO administration


**Total employer cost** **12% + 0.50% + 0.50% = 13%** Various accounts


The employer’s contributions do not appear as deductions on the employee’s salary slip because they are paid separately by the employer. However, some salary slips show them as information items in a separate section.


For a detailed understanding of when PF becomes applicable, read our[guide to minimum employees for PF, ESI, gratuity, and bonus](https://salarybox.in/blog/minimum-employees-pf-esi-gratuity-bonus-india/) .


### 2. ESI (Employee State Insurance) Contribution


Aspect Details


What it is A social security scheme providing medical and cash benefits to employees


Employee contribution 0.75% of gross salary


Employer contribution 3.25% of gross salary (not deducted from employee, paid separately)


Applicability Employees earning gross salary up to ₹21,000 per month in establishments with 10 or more employees


Tax treatment Employee ESI contribution is not eligible for Section 80C deduction


**Calculation Example:** If Gross Salary = ₹18,000: Employee ESI = ₹18,000 × 0.75% = ₹135 per month Employer ESI = ₹18,000 × 3.25% = ₹585 per month (not deducted from employee)


**Important:** Once an employee’s gross salary crosses ₹21,000 per month, ESI deduction stops from the next contribution period (April or October).


### 3. Professional Tax (PT)


Aspect Details


What it is A state government tax on salaried individuals and professionals


Maximum limit ₹2,500 per year (as per Article 276 of the Constitution)


Applicability Only in states that levy Professional Tax


Tax treatment Fully deductible from taxable income under Section 16(iii)


**State Wise Professional Tax Slabs (Common Examples)**


**Maharashtra:**


Monthly Salary Monthly PT


Up to ₹7,500 Nil


₹7,501 to ₹10,000 ₹175


Above ₹10,000 ₹200 (₹300 in February)


**Karnataka:**


Monthly Salary Monthly PT


Up to ₹15,000 Nil


₹15,001 to ₹25,000 ₹200


Above ₹25,000 ₹200 (with annual total of ₹2,400)


**West Bengal:**


Monthly Salary Monthly PT


Up to ₹10,000 Nil


₹10,001 to ₹15,000 ₹110


₹15,001 to ₹25,000 ₹130


₹25,001 to ₹40,000 ₹150


Above ₹40,000 ₹200


**States with No Professional Tax:** Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir


### 4. TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) on Salary


Aspect Details


What it is Income tax deducted by the employer before paying salary


Legal basis Section 192 of the Income Tax Act


Calculation method Employer projects annual salary, applies the chosen tax regime’s slabs, and divides the annual tax equally across 12 months


Employee’s role Must declare their preferred tax regime (old or new) and submit investment proofs under the old regime


**New Tax Regime Slabs (AY 2026-27, Default Regime):**


Annual Income Tax Rate


Up to ₹4,00,000 Nil


₹4,00,001 to ₹8,00,000 5%


₹8,00,001 to ₹12,00,000 10%


₹12,00,001 to ₹16,00,000 15%


₹16,00,001 to ₹20,00,000 20%


₹20,00,001 to ₹24,00,000 25%


Above ₹24,00,000 30%


Standard deduction of ₹75,000 is available under the new regime from AY 2025-26 onwards. The rebate under Section 87A makes income up to ₹12,00,000 (approximately ₹12,75,000 with standard deduction) effectively tax free.


**Old Tax Regime Slabs (AY 2026-27):**


Annual Income Tax Rate


Up to ₹2,50,000 Nil


₹2,50,001 to ₹5,00,000 5%


₹5,00,001 to ₹10,00,000 20%


Above ₹10,00,000 30%


Standard deduction of ₹50,000 under the old regime. Additional deductions under Section 80C (₹1,50,000), 80D (health insurance), HRA exemption, and others are available only under the old regime.


**TDS Calculation Example (New Regime):** Employee with annual CTC of ₹8,00,000 (Gross Salary approximately ₹7,20,000 after employer PF):


Step Calculation


Gross salary ₹7,20,000


Standard deduction minus ₹75,000


Taxable income ₹6,45,000


Tax on first ₹4,00,000 Nil


Tax on ₹2,45,000 at 5% ₹12,250


Total tax ₹12,250


Health and education cess (4%) ₹490


Total annual tax ₹12,740


Monthly TDS ₹12,740 / 12 = ₹1,062


### 5. Other Common Deductions


Deduction What It Is How It Appears


Loan recovery EMI for salary advance or company loan Fixed monthly deduction


Leave without pay (LOP) Salary deduction for unapproved absence (Daily salary × LOP days)


Notice period recovery Deduction if employee leaves without serving full notice One time deduction in full and final


Canteen charges Subsidized meal facility charges Fixed monthly amount


Union dues Trade union membership fees Small fixed amount


Insurance premium Group health or life insurance employee share Fixed monthly or annual deduction


NPS (National Pension System) Voluntary retirement savings under NPS Tier 1 10% of basic (employer) + voluntary employee contribution


### Complete Deductions Summary Table


Here is what the deductions section looks like for the same ₹50,000 CTC employee:


Deduction Component Monthly Amount


Provident Fund (Employee 12%) ₹2,400


ESI (Employee 0.75%) Nil (gross exceeds ₹21,000)


Professional Tax (Maharashtra) ₹200


TDS (Income Tax) ₹1,062


**Total Deductions** **₹3,662**


## Complete Salary Slip Example: Putting It All Together


Let us now create a complete salary slip for a real scenario.


**Employee:** Priya Mehta, Software Developer **Company:** TechStar Solutions Pvt. Ltd., Pune **Monthly CTC:** ₹75,000 **Tax Regime:** New Tax Regime


### Earnings Side


Component Monthly Amount


Basic Salary ₹30,000


House Rent Allowance (HRA) ₹15,000


Special Allowance ₹18,850


Conveyance Allowance ₹1,600


Medical Allowance ₹1,250


Children Education Allowance ₹200


**Gross Earnings** **₹66,900**


### Employer Cost (Not Deducted from Employee)


Component Monthly Amount


Employer PF (12% of Basic) ₹3,600


Employer ESI Nil (gross exceeds ₹21,000)


EDLI (0.50% of Basic) ₹150


PF Admin (0.50% of Basic) ₹150


Gratuity provision (4.81% of Basic) ₹1,443


Group health insurance (employer share) ₹750


**Total Employer Cost Beyond Gross** **₹6,093**


Note: Gross Earnings (₹66,900) + Employer Costs (₹6,093) = Approximately ₹72,993. The small difference from ₹75,000 CTC accounts for variable components or one time annual benefits.


### Deductions Side


Component Monthly Amount


Provident Fund (Employee 12% of Basic) ₹3,600


ESI (Employee) Nil


Professional Tax (Maharashtra) ₹200


TDS (Income Tax, New Regime) ₹3,150


**Total Deductions** **₹6,950**


### Net Pay Calculation


Item Amount


Gross Earnings ₹66,900


Total Deductions ₹6,950


**Net Pay (Take Home Salary)** **₹59,950**


This is the amount credited to Priya’s bank account on the payment date.

## Salary Slip Format for Different Salary Levels


Different salary levels have different components and deductions. Here is how salary slips look across three common salary ranges in India:


### Comparison: ₹15,000 vs ₹35,000 vs ₹80,000 Monthly CTC


Component ₹15,000 CTC (Delivery Associate) ₹35,000 CTC (Office Executive) ₹80,000 CTC (Senior Developer)


Basic Salary ₹6,000 ₹14,000 ₹32,000


HRA ₹3,000 ₹7,000 ₹16,000


Special Allowance ₹3,130 ₹9,720 ₹20,200


Other Allowances ₹400 ₹1,600 ₹3,050


**Gross Earnings** **₹12,530** **₹32,320** **₹71,250**


Employee PF (12% of Basic) ₹720 ₹1,680 ₹3,840


Employee ESI (0.75% of Gross) ₹94 Nil (gross above ₹21,000) Nil


Professional Tax Nil (below threshold) ₹200 ₹200


TDS Nil (income below taxable limit) ₹850 ₹5,200


**Total Deductions** **₹814** **₹2,730** **₹9,240**


**Net Pay (Take Home)** **₹11,716** **₹29,590** **₹62,010**


### Key Observations Across Salary Levels


Observation Explanation


ESI applies only at ₹15,000 CTC level Because gross salary is under ₹21,000 threshold


TDS is zero at ₹15,000 level Annual income falls below the taxable threshold under the new regime


PT varies Depends on state and whether gross crosses the state’s threshold


Take home percentage decreases as salary increases Higher salaries attract more PF and TDS deductions


CTC Level Take Home Percentage


₹15,000 CTC ~78% of CTC


₹35,000 CTC ~85% of CTC


₹80,000 CTC ~78% of CTC


The “sweet spot” for take home percentage is typically in the ₹25,000 to ₹50,000 CTC range, where PF is moderate and TDS is relatively low.


## How to Read Your Salary Slip: A 6 Step Checklist


Use this checklist every month to verify your salary slip is accurate:


Step What to Check What to Look For


1 Verify your personal details Name, employee ID, PAN, UAN, bank account (should all match your records)


2 Check the pay period and payment date Ensure it matches the correct month and the date salary was credited


3 Verify gross earnings Add up all earnings components; they should total the gross salary figure


4 Verify each deduction PF should be 12% of basic; ESI should be 0.75% of gross (if applicable); PT should match your state slab


5 Check net pay against bank credit Net pay on the slip should exactly match the amount credited to your account


6 Review YTD (Year to Date) figures Running totals of earnings, PF, TDS, and other deductions should accumulate correctly from April


### Common Salary Slip Errors to Watch For


Error How to Spot It Impact


PF calculated on wrong base PF amount is not exactly 12% of basic Over or under contribution affecting retirement corpus


LOP not matching actual leaves LOP deduction present when you had approved leaves Unnecessary salary reduction


Wrong Professional Tax slab PT amount does not match your state’s slab for your salary level Overpayment or underpayment of state tax


Missing arrears Salary revision was announced but arrears not paid Lost income


HRA mismatch HRA on payslip differs from offer letter Tax exemption calculation affected


Old tax regime TDS applied despite choosing new regime TDS amount seems higher than expected Excess tax deducted, cash flow impacted


## What Employers Must Include in a Salary Slip (Legal Requirements)


If you are a business owner or HR professional, here is the minimum information your salary slip must contain to be legally compliant:


### Mandatory Fields


Field Required Under Penalty for Non Compliance


Employee name and ID S&E Acts, Code on Wages Fine varies by state


Pay period (month/year) S&E Acts Fine varies by state


Gross wages Payment of Wages Act Up to ₹7,500


All deductions with description Payment of Wages Act, Section 13A Up to ₹7,500


Net wages paid Payment of Wages Act Up to ₹7,500


PF contribution (employee and employer) EPF Act Section 14 prosecution


ESI contribution (if applicable) ESI Act Section 85 prosecution


TDS deducted Income Tax Act, Section 192 Penalty under Section 271C


### Best Practice Additional Fields


Field Why Include It


Company name, logo, address Professionalism and document credibility


Employee PAN and UAN Helps employee track PF and file taxes


Bank account details (masked) Verification reference


Leave balance Transparency on remaining entitled leaves


YTD (Year to Date) totals Running totals for tax planning


Employer PF and ESI contributions Full transparency on total employment cost


Working days and LOP days Justifies any attendance based deductions


## CTC vs Gross Salary vs Net Salary: How They Connect on the Salary Slip


One of the most confusing aspects of Indian salary slips is the difference between CTC, gross salary, and net salary. Here is how they relate:


Term What It Includes Appears on Salary Slip?


CTC (Cost to Company) Gross salary + employer PF + employer ESI + gratuity + insurance + any other employer costs Not directly (CTC is an annual figure in the offer letter)


Gross Salary Basic + HRA + all allowances + bonuses Yes (total of all earnings components)


Net Salary (Take Home) Gross salary minus all deductions (PF, ESI, PT, TDS, others) Yes (the amount credited to bank)


### The Flow from CTC to Net Salary


Step Description Example (₹6 LPA CTC)


Annual CTC Total company cost per year ₹6,00,000


Minus employer PF (12% of Basic) Employer’s PF contribution minus ₹28,800


Minus employer ESI (if applicable) Employer’s ESI contribution minus ₹0 (not applicable)


Minus gratuity provision 4.81% of Basic minus ₹11,544


Minus insurance and other employer costs Group health insurance, etc. minus ₹6,000


= Annual Gross Salary What the employee “earns” on paper ₹5,53,656


Monthly Gross Salary Annual Gross / 12 ₹46,138


Minus employee PF (12% of Basic) Employee’s PF contribution minus ₹2,400


Minus Professional Tax State tax minus ₹200


Minus TDS Income tax minus ₹600


= Monthly Net Salary (Take Home) Amount credited to bank ₹42,938

## Salary Slip and Income Tax: What You Need to Know


Your salary slip is the primary document for income tax purposes. Here is how different salary slip components affect your tax filing:


### Components and Their Tax Treatment Summary


Component Taxable Under New Regime? Taxable Under Old Regime? Deduction/Exemption Available?


Basic Salary Yes Yes No


HRA Yes Partially Section 10(13A) exemption (old regime only)


Special Allowance Yes Yes No


DA Yes Yes No


Conveyance Allowance Yes Yes Standard deduction replaces old exemption


LTA Yes Partially Section 10(5) exemption (old regime only)


Medical Allowance Yes Yes No (old ₹15,000 exemption discontinued)


Employee PF No (exempt) No (exempt) Section 80C deduction (old regime)


Professional Tax Deductible Deductible Section 16(iii)


Standard Deduction ₹75,000 ₹50,000 Automatic; no proof needed


### Which Tax Regime Is Better?


Scenario Better Regime Why


CTC under ₹12 lakh, no investments New Regime Zero tax with rebate, no proof submission needed


CTC ₹12 to ₹20 lakh, heavy investments (PPF, NPS, home loan, HRA) Old Regime Multiple deductions reduce taxable income significantly


CTC above ₹20 lakh, few deductions New Regime Lower slab rates compensate for missing deductions


Employee unsure New Regime (default) Simpler, no investment proof needed


## Salary Slip for Special Situations


### Full and Final Settlement Slip


When an employee resigns or is terminated, the final salary slip includes additional components:


Component Included in F&F Salary Slip


Salary for days worked in the last month Prorated basic, HRA, allowances


Leave encashment Unused earned leave × daily salary


Gratuity (if eligible) 15 days salary × years of service / 26 (for 5+ years of service)


Notice period recovery or payout Deduction if notice not served; payout if waived by employer


Bonus (prorated) If applicable under Bonus Act


Pending reimbursements Travel, medical, or other approved claims


### Salary Slip During Probation

## Frequently Asked Questions


### 1. What is a salary slip and what should it contain?


A salary slip (also called a payslip) is a monthly document issued by an employer showing the detailed breakdown of an employee’s salary. It must contain: employee name and ID, pay period, all earnings components (basic salary, HRA, allowances), all deductions (PF, ESI, Professional Tax, TDS), gross salary, total deductions, and net pay (the amount credited to the bank account). It should also include the employee’s PAN, UAN number, and bank account details.


### 2. Is it legal for an employer to not give a salary slip in India?


No. While the central Payment of Wages Act does not explicitly use the term “salary slip,” most state Shops and Establishments Acts mandate that employers provide a written wage statement to employees. Several states have prescribed specific forms (like Form T in Tamil Nadu and Form XIX in Karnataka). The Code on Wages, 2019, when fully notified, will make salary slips mandatory for all employers across India.


### 3. How is net salary calculated from gross salary?


Net salary is calculated by subtracting all deductions from gross salary. The formula is: Net Salary = Gross Salary minus Employee PF minus Employee ESI (if applicable) minus Professional Tax minus TDS minus any other deductions (loan recovery, LOP, etc.). For example, if gross salary is ₹46,250 and total deductions are ₹3,662, the net salary (take home) is ₹42,588.


### 4. What is the difference between CTC and gross salary on a salary slip?


CTC (Cost to Company) includes everything the employer spends on you: gross salary plus employer PF contribution plus employer ESI plus gratuity provision plus insurance and any other benefits. Gross salary is only the earnings portion before deductions. For a ₹6 lakh CTC, the gross salary might be around ₹5.5 lakh after removing employer PF, gratuity, and insurance. Only gross salary and deductions appear on the salary slip; CTC is mentioned in the offer letter.


### 5. How is HRA exemption calculated for tax purposes?


HRA exemption under Section 10(13A) is the lowest of three amounts: (a) actual HRA received, (b) 50% of basic salary in metro cities or 40% in non metro cities, and (c) actual rent paid minus 10% of basic salary. This exemption is available only under the old tax regime. Under the new tax regime, the entire HRA is taxable. Employees must submit rent receipts and the landlord’s PAN (if annual rent exceeds ₹1 lakh) to claim HRA exemption.


### 6. Why is my PF deduction different from my colleague’s even though we have the same salary?


PF can be calculated on the full basic salary or restricted to the statutory ceiling of ₹15,000. If your employer calculates PF on the actual basic (say ₹25,000), your PF deduction will be ₹3,000. If your colleague’s previous employer was calculating on ₹15,000, their deduction was ₹1,800. Some employers offer a choice between restricted and full PF. Additionally, if basic salary percentages differ in your respective salary structures, PF amounts will vary even with the same CTC.


### 7. What should I do if I find an error in my salary slip?


First, identify the specific discrepancy by checking each component against your offer letter and previous payslips. Then, raise the issue with your HR or payroll department in writing (email is best for documentation). Common errors include wrong PF base calculation, incorrect LOP deductions, missing overtime or incentive payments, and wrong Professional Tax slab. Most payroll errors can be corrected in the next month’s salary through an arrears payment. If HR does not respond, you can escalate to the labour department or file a complaint under the Payment of Wages Act.


### 8. Can I use a salary slip to apply for a home loan?


Yes. Salary slips are one of the primary documents banks require for home loan applications. Most banks ask for salary slips from the last 3 to 6 months along with bank statements showing salary credits. The bank uses your salary slip to verify your net monthly income, check the stability of your earnings, and calculate your loan eligibility (typically, EMI should not exceed 40% to 50% of your net monthly salary). A clearly formatted salary slip with all components visible speeds up the loan approval process.


## Conclusion


Understanding your salary slip is not just about knowing how much money hits your bank account every month. It is about verifying that your employer is making the correct PF contributions toward your retirement, deducting the right amount of tax, and paying you every component promised in your offer letter.


For employees: use the 6 step checklist in this guide to review your payslip every month. Catching an error early is much easier than correcting it months later.


For employers: a professional, accurate salary slip builds trust with your team and keeps you compliant with Indian labour laws.
